title: Effective AI Agents Need Data Flywheels, Not The Next Biggest LLM –  Sylendran Arunagiri, NVIDIA
talk_summary: NVIDIA's Sylendran Arunagiri argues agents stay effective via a data flywheel: capture production logs and user feedback, curate ground truth, then fine-tune and evaluate smaller models to replace large ones. Their internal employee-support router agent went from a 70B model at 96% accuracy/26s latency to a fine-tuned 8B matching accuracy and a 1B at 94%, using only ~685 curated data points.

takeaways.technique: Fine-tune small models on curated routing/decision data to replace big models
takeaways.what_they_do: They collected ~685 ground-truth examples from production feedback and fine-tuned 8B/3B/1B variants to match a 70B router's accuracy at far lower latency and cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just with 685 data points the results that we achieved were outstanding
takeaways.numbers: 70B: 96% acc, 26s first-token; 8B fine-tuned matches 96%; 1B: 94%; 98% inference cost savings, 70x lower latency

takeaways.technique: LLM-as-judge to triage failures, then human SME to confirm true errors
takeaways.what_they_do: They used an LLM judge to investigate 495 unsatisfactory responses, found 140 routing errors, then SMEs confirmed only 32 were truly routing faults, building a clean ground-truth set.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we found out 32 of them were truly due to this incorrect routing
takeaways.numbers: 495 unsatisfactory -> 140 flagged by judge -> 32 confirmed by SME

takeaways.technique: Feedback capture loop on production traffic
takeaways.what_they_do: They circulated feedback forms to employees on real queries, labeling responses satisfactory/unsatisfactory to seed the flywheel.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we asked employees to submit few queries and capture uh the feedback in terms of whether the the response was useful to them or not

takeaways.technique: Router agent over domain expert agents
takeaways.what_they_do: A cheap LLM router classifies intent and dispatches to specialized expert agents each backed by a RAG pipeline, rather than one monolithic agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the router agent depending on the user query understands the intent and context and guides or routes the query to one of these expert agents

takeaways.technique: Periodic re-evaluation to promote smaller models as new ones ship
takeaways.what_they_do: They run a recurring evaluate-and-fine-tune cycle so that when a smaller/cheaper model meets target accuracy it gets promoted into production.
takeaways.evidence_quote: imagine building an automated loop or a cycle of continuous and periodic evaluation and fine-tuning as newer models are published

takeaways.technique: Error attribution before scaling model size
takeaways.what_they_do: They warn against concluding 'need bigger model' from raw accuracy gaps; instead they attribute failures to root causes (routing vs retrieval vs model) before deciding.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that's exactly where most of the enterprise evaluations get it wrong
takeaways.numbers: 8B baseline was <14% vs 70B 96%, yet fine-tuning closed the gap
